title: Huasteca Potosina in December: What's Open Over the Holidays, Prices and Weather
metaTitle: Huasteca Potosina in December: What's Open & Prices
metaDescription: Visiting Huasteca Potosina in December? Opening hours, real prices, weather, what's open on Christmas and New Year's, and the best tours for your holiday trip.
excerpt: What's open, opening hours, real prices and weather in the Huasteca Potosina during the December holidays, plus a suggested 3-day itinerary.
contentHtml:
The Huasteca Potosina in December is a region in east-central Mexico where waterfalls, canyons and lowland forest stay open to the public through the entire year-end holiday season. Many travelers assume the attractions close for Christmas or New Year's, but that's not the case: the vast majority operate as usual. In December, the Huasteca Potosina welcomes families, couples and groups who take advantage of the dry weather to reach places that call for more caution during the rainy season.

This guide tells you exactly what's open, the hours, and what each attraction costs during the December holidays in the Huasteca. You'll find verified prices for 2026, real temperatures for December weather in the Huasteca, and a selection of organized tours so you don't waste time arranging transportation on your own. According to local operators in the region, December accounts for 18 to 22 % of total annual visitors, second only to July and August.

At www.huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators in the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who explore the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: November 2026. If your dates are already set, check out the all-inclusive packages to visit the Huasteca Potosina in December.

Which attractions are open in the Huasteca Potosina in December

Tamul Waterfall: access, boat ride and hours during the Christmas season

Tamul Waterfall (Cascada de Tamul), with a 105-meter drop, is the tallest in San Luis Potosí and one of the most popular destinations during the December holidays in the Huasteca. In December the Tampaón River runs lower than in the rainy season, so the water looks more turquoise and the trip by panga (wooden canoe) is more comfortable. Admission is $220 MXN per person plus an additional $300 MXN for the panga ride. Both are cash only, so bring bills from Ciudad Valles.

The groups we coordinate to Tamul leave early to make the most of the morning light and avoid the crowds that build after 10:00 a.m., especially between December 23 and January 1. To visit the waterfall with transportation included, rappelling in front of the wall of water and a trip through the Tampaón canyon, book the Tamul Waterfall Rappel from $2,450 MXN per person.

Micos Waterfalls, Puente de Dios and Sótano de las Huahuas: real hours

The Micos Waterfalls (Cascadas de Micos) are open every day from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. in December, including December 25 and January 1. General admission is $100 MXN; activities like the zip line, kayaking and skybike are paid separately on site. Puente de Dios, in Tamasopo, charges $150 MXN per person and keeps the area's standard attraction hours: 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. The Sótano de las Huahuas cave, in Aquismón, charges $100 MXN admission. At sunset, parrots and swifts return to the 478-meter-deep pit, a show that doesn't depend on the holiday calendar.

To combine Tamul, the Sótano de las Huahuas at sunset and the Cenote Cueva del Agua in a single day, check out the Tamul Expedition from $1,550 MXN per person. If you're more interested in the freshwater route to Puente de Dios, read our guide to Puente de Dios in Tamasopo.

Huasteca weather in December: temperatures, rain and river conditions

What's the December weather like in the Huasteca lowlands and mountains?

December weather in the Huasteca splits into two clear microclimates. In the lowlands — Ciudad Valles, Tamasopo, Aquismón — daytime temperatures hover around 22–26 °C, with nights that can drop to 12–14 °C. It's the dry season, so the chance of rain is low and the rivers show their most intense turquoise of the year. In the high mountains of Xilitla and La Trinidad, mornings can be between 8 and 14 °C, with frequent fog before 9:00 a.m. that clears toward midday.

First-time December visitors are often surprised by how cold nights get in Xilitla. A light jacket or a thin rain layer makes all the difference. The good news: December weather in the Huasteca is the most stable of the year for hiking, since the ground is firm and the trails don't have the mud of the wet season. see available tours in the Huasteca Potosina

How much does it cost to visit the Huasteca Potosina in December with a tour?

Guided day tours run between $900 and $1,950 MXN per person in 2026, depending on the destination and whether breakfast is included. Packages with lodging start at $8,699 MXN per couple for 3 days and 2 nights with breakfasts, tours, admission fees and certified guides. These packages are especially useful during the December holidays in the Huasteca, because hotels in Ciudad Valles and Xilitla raise their rates by 20 to 30 % during the week of December 24 to January 1.

To compare lodging options with built-in tours, check the available packages or read our article on how much a trip to the Huasteca Potosina costs, with a breakdown by type of traveler.

Practical tips before traveling to the Huasteca Potosina in December

Traveling to the Huasteca at Christmas takes different logistics than the rest of the year. Roads to Xilitla, Aquismón and Tamasopo can get jammed between December 22 and January 2, and the parking lots at Micos and Tamul fill up before 9:00 a.m. on those days. Booking ahead and leaving your hotel early cuts your wait time at each attraction significantly.

  • Book at least 10 days ahead: during the December holidays in the Huasteca, tours with limited spots (rafting, rappelling, RZR) sell out fast. Confirm your spot before December 15.
  • Always carry cash: Tamul Waterfall charges $300 MXN for the panga, cash only, and many parking lots and food stands in the area don't take cards either. Plan on at least $800–1,000 MXN extra in small bills.
  • Pack for two climates: wear quick-dry clothes for the rivers and bring a warm layer for nights in Xilitla. Check the packing checklist for the Potosí jungle so you don't forget anything.
  • Sunscreen and bug repellent: the December sun in the lowlands is strong between 10:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. Repellent is a must near pools and springs, even if it hasn't rained recently.
  • Leave before 7:30 a.m. on holidays: December 25 and January 1 are the busiest days at Micos and Puente de Dios. Reaching the parking lot before 8:00 a.m. means getting in without long waits.

Suggested 3-day itinerary for the December holidays in the Huasteca

The groups we host in December usually have 3 to 5 days. With 3 full days you can combine the Tamasopo water route, the bird experience at the Huahuas and the Xilitla mountains without rushing. The most practical base is Ciudad Valles for the first two days and Xilitla for the third. They're about 90 km apart on the federal highway, a 1 h 45 min drive.

Day 1: water route and waterfalls from Ciudad Valles

Spend the first day on the freshwater route: Puente de Dios ($150 MXN), the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo (Seven Waterfalls of Tamasopo) and the Micos Waterfalls ($100 MXN). According to local guides, this circuit takes a comfortable 8–9 hours leaving Ciudad Valles at 7:30 a.m. To do it without worrying about transportation or access, book the Water Route from $1,600 MXN per person, including transportation and a certified guide.

Day 2: Tamul and Sótano de las Huahuas

Day two pairs Tamul Waterfall in the morning with the Sótano de las Huahuas at sunset. Both are in the same direction from Ciudad Valles toward Aquismón, which saves unnecessary driving. The bird flight at the Huahuas happens between 5:30 and 6:30 p.m. in December, depending on the weather. Arriving with 30 minutes to spare is enough to get the best viewing angle. To learn more about the birds' behavior and the difference between the region's two caves, read our article on Sótano de las Golondrinas vs. Sótano de las Huahuas.

FAQ about the Huasteca Potosina in December

Which attractions close on December 25 and January 1 in the Huasteca Potosina?

Most natural attractions — Micos Waterfalls, Puente de Dios, Tamul and the Sótano de las Huahuas — stay open on December 25 and January 1 in 2026, with their usual hours of 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Arrive before 9:00 a.m. on those days because of the heavy crowds.

How much does a 3-day trip to the Huasteca Potosina cost in December?

A 3-day, 2-night package with lodging, breakfasts, tours and certified guides starts at $8,699 MXN per couple in 2026. If you travel independently, budget $1,500–2,000 MXN per person per day for admission fees, transportation and basic meals.

Is December a good time to visit the Huasteca Potosina?

Yes. December is the dry season, with temperatures of 22–26 °C in the lowlands and rivers with turquoise water. The trails aren't muddy and river flow is more manageable for water activities. The Xilitla mountains can have mornings of 8–14 °C, so bring a warm layer.

Is it safe to travel to the Huasteca Potosina at Christmas with family or as a couple?

The Huasteca at Christmas is a safe option for families and couples who stick to established tourist routes. Drive during daylight, use operators with certified guides and book lodging ahead of time. For detailed road tips, read our guide to road safety in the Huasteca Potosina.
